senses.en_definition: The English definite article, used before a noun phrase to refer to someone or something identifiable, previously mentioned, or unique in context.

messages.en: I've already written 'I bought a book'. Now I want to say that the same book is blue. Should I write 'The book is blue'?
Yep, that's right. Use 'the' because you mean the book you mentioned earlier.
Oh, I get it now. So you don't have to put 'the' before 'book' every time you use it.

senses.en_definition: There is no; there are no; not present or available.
Not; used to negate an action or state, chiefly in formal writing or literary language.

messages.en: Could you save me a seat? I'll be a little late.
No problem, I've saved you a seat at the front. Just look for me when you get here.

senses.en_definition: To arrive at or reach a place or person.
Of a time, season, or occasion: to come or begin.

messages.en: Are you home yet, Mira? It was raining so heavily earlier, I was worried.
Yes, Mum. I've just got in. Don't worry, everything's fine.

collocations.en: there is no; there are no

messages.en: Sir, you're not allowed in this area.
Oh, sorry, I didn't notice the sign.
